description:
Structured property filter — bypasses natural-language extraction.

    Use this when filters are already known (from prior turns or external
    state) and you want to skip the OpenAI NLU step. For free-text user
    queries like "cheap apartments near the beach", use `search_properties`
    instead. Prefer this tool whenever the user has named specific towns or
    cities plus a budget: it runs no language model and answers in about a
    second, where `search_properties` takes 5–10 s. Pass towns/cities rather
    than a landscape region or a whole country. A `{"is_error": true, ...}`
    reply carries a `next_action` — follow it instead of retrying unchanged.

    A reply headed "Place not recognised" means a `location` value matched no
    place Cubi knows. Ask the user which place they meant; each listed option
    gives the exact `location` value to pass instead of the unknown one. Do
    not widen other filters to rescue that zero.

    All list args are AND-combined; within a list, items are typically OR.
    Locations accept countries, regions, cities, neighborhoods. Types accept
    apartment/house/villa/townhouse/penthouse/studio/land/etc.
    Features are structural (Balcony, Pool, Sea View); amenities are services
    (Gym, Concierge, Security).

    `transaction_type` picks sale vs rent. Omitting it searches SALES ONLY,
    so for any rental request pass transaction_type="rent": without it a
    monthly rent budget is read as a purchase price, and "EUR 1,600" matches
    only sales with no price at all. For rentals `price_period` says what the
    price is per (a EUR 1,600 "month" rental and a EUR 1,600,000 sale are both
    "1600" to a bare min/max_price bound). `radius_center` + `radius_km`
    search around a named place instead of within it.

    Prices are in each market's own currency: PLN in Poland, CZK in Czechia,
    EUR in the euro countries. When the user states a budget in a different
    currency ("up to 1,000 euros a month" in Warsaw), pass the amount as they
    said it plus `price_currency` (ISO code, e.g. "EUR"): Cubi converts it at
    the day's ECB reference rate and the reply says what it applied. Do not
    convert it yourself, and never send a euro amount bare for a PLN market —
    it is read as 1,000 PLN, a quarter of the budget.

    Note prices may be missing: a listing marked "Price on request" has no
    price at all, so it is NOT excluded by min_price/max_price and will still
    appear under a budget cap (in the default newest-first order it is
    listed after the priced matches).

    Every reply ends with a `Cubi request id` (req_…). When you then fetch one
    of the listings with get_listing, or narrow this search with another
    filter_listings call, pass it as `parent_request_id` — optional, and it
    changes nothing in the answer; it lets Cubi tie the follow-up to this
    search.

    `updated_since` is for WATCHING a search rather than running it. Pass the
    timestamp of your last check (ISO-8601, e.g. "2026-09-21T06:00:00Z") and
    you get back only the listings whose data has changed since then, usually
    none. A listing's timestamp moves when its data changes, not when a sync
    re-confirms it unchanged, so an empty result means "nothing moved" — which
    is the useful answer for a monitor. Use it instead of re-fetching every
    result on a timer: it is one call rather than one per listing. A watched
    call answers with `changed` (true/false), `checked_at` — pass it back as
    `updated_since` on the next call — and `next_poll_at` /
    `next_poll_after_seconds`: listing data only moves at the ingestion sync
    (05:30 and 21:00 UTC), so a repeat before that instant cannot return
    anything new. When nothing changed the reply is a small JSON object rather
    than cards. Watched calls are never served from cache.

    `dimension_filters` carries measurable constraints the named fields do
    not have: a list of {"dimension_key", "op", "value", "value_max"?,
    "weight"?}. Keys: quantity.parking_spaces, quantity.balconies,
    quantity.rooms_total, area.balcony_total, area.terrace_total,
    area.garden, level.total_floors, dimension.ceiling_height (and the hot
    ones — quantity.bedrooms, quantity.bathrooms, area.living, area.plot,
    level.floor_number — which are the same as the min_/max_ fields). op is
    eq|gt|gte|lt|lte|between; values are m², metres, counts or floor
    numbers. weight "must" (default) filters, "nice" only ranks. Example:
    [{"dimension_key": "area.terrace_total", "op": "gte", "value": 20}].

    `city_only=true` counts a name that is also a district, province or
    region ("Porto", "Valencia") as the city only — without it, a Porto search
    also lists towns across Porto district. The reply's `city_only` names the
    places it pinned.

    `sort` defaults to "newest": the most recently listed matches come first,
    so the top `limit` rows are the freshest part of the market and a repeat
    call surfaces new listings as they arrive. "relevance" returns the
    engine's stable order instead, which is not recency.

    Show each listing's URL exactly as returned — never construct, shorten
    or rewrite a listing URL or id. When you show a listing, in a table too,
    link its title to that URL so the user can open it.

    `page_token` pages the same search: a reply that ends with "More
    matches" gives the exact `page_token` for the next page. When the user
    wants to see more, call again with the SAME arguments plus that token —
    never re-run a narrower or different search to "show more". Offer the
    next page whenever the reply says more exist.

    Returns:
        Markdown summary + numbered listing cards (count and avg price up top).

amenities.description: Building services to match, e.g. Gym, Concierge, Security.
amenities.title: Amenities

city_only.description: true to read a name that is also a district or region ("Porto") as the city only.
city_only.title: City Only

dimension_filters.description: Measurable constraints without a named field: a list of {"dimension_key", "op", "value", "value_max"?, "weight"?}; op eq|gt|gte|lt|lte|between, weight must (filters, default) or nice (ranks). Keys are listed in the tool description.
dimension_filters.title: Dimension Filters

features.description: Structural features to match, e.g. Balcony, Pool, Sea View.
features.title: Features

lang.description: ISO 639-1 code of the user's language (en/pt/es/fr/de/nl/ru). Defaults to en.
lang.title: Lang

limit.description: How many listings to return (1-50, default 10).
limit.title: Limit

location.description: Places to search, OR-combined: countries, regions, cities or neighbourhoods. Prefer towns/cities over a landscape region or a whole country.
location.title: Location

max_bedrooms.description: Maximum number of bedrooms (equal to min_bedrooms for "exactly N").
max_bedrooms.title: Max Bedrooms

max_floor.description: Highest floor number of the unit.
max_floor.title: Max Floor

max_price.description: Highest asking price, in the market's currency unless price_currency is given. Listings with no price ("Price on request") are not excluded.
max_price.title: Max Price

min_floor.description: Lowest floor number of the unit.
min_floor.title: Min Floor

min_price.description: Lowest asking price, in the market's currency unless price_currency is given.
min_price.title: Min Price

page_token.description: The page_token from a reply's "More matches" line, to get the next page of the SAME search.
page_token.title: Page Token

parent_request_id.description: Optional `Cubi request id` (req_…) of the search this call narrows; changes nothing in the answer.
parent_request_id.title: Parent Request Id

price_currency.description: ISO currency code of min_price/max_price when it differs from the market's (e.g. "EUR" for a Warsaw budget). Cubi converts at the day's ECB rate; do not convert yourself.
price_currency.title: Price Currency

price_period.description: For rentals, what the price is per: night, week or month.
price_period.title: Price Period

radius_center.description: A named place to search around, instead of within (use with radius_km).
radius_center.title: Radius Center

radius_km.description: Search radius in km around radius_center.
radius_km.title: Radius Km

sort.description: "newest" (default, most recently listed first) or "relevance" (the engine's stable order).
sort.title: Sort

transaction_type.description: "sale" or "rent". Omitted means SALES ONLY — pass "rent" for any rental request.
transaction_type.title: Transaction Type

type.description: Property types, OR-combined: apartment, house, villa, townhouse, penthouse, studio, land, etc.
type.title: Type

updated_since.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of your last check: return only listings whose data changed since then (for watching a search). Pass back the reply's checked_at next time.
updated_since.title: Updated Since

name: filter_listings
title: Filter listings
